request.prompt:
You are extracting the numeric claims of one section of a model-validation report, so that each
can be checked against the artifact it cites. Section: data_integrity.

The prose is printed below one line per line, each prefixed with its own number and a vertical
bar. List EVERY number that appears in the prose, in the order it appears, including numbers that
appear inside a citation's logical name and numbers written with a thousands separator or a per
cent sign. For each one:

- "line" is the number printed to the left of the line the number appears on. Give the number
  only; do not copy the line's text back, and do not count the prefix itself as a number.
- "value" is the number as written, with thousands separators and the per cent sign removed:
  "3,500" is 3500, "22.0%" is 22.0.
- "unit" is "percent" when the number is written with a per cent sign, "count" for a number of
  rows, features or events, "currency", "bp" for basis points, "months" for a horizon, and
  "ratio" for every other dimensionless quantity (AUC, PSI, VIF, a coefficient, a lift).
- "metric" is what the number measures, taken from the logical name of the artifact it cites
  (auc, brier, psi, vif, calibration_slope, delta_auc, coefficient, event_rate, ...), or null.
- "split" is train, test, out_of_time or vintage_holdout, or null.
- "comparison" is "eq" for a number that equals its artifact; "delta" for a difference written
  "from a to b" or "a gap of x", whose value is the second cited artifact minus the first; and
  "ratio" for a number written as one artifact divided by another. A delta or ratio carries TWO
  adjacent citations, in that order.
- "citation" is the [[art:...]] token the number carries, copied exactly, or null when the
  sentence carries none. Do not invent a citation and do not move one from another number.
- "rounding" is the number of decimals the prose wrote when it wrote fewer than the artifact has
  (2 for a lift written 2.24), or null.

Return every number even when it has no citation: a number you leave out is still counted, and
counted against the report.

Prose:
 1| Model testing is a core component of development that includes a critical assessment of data quality, relevance, and inputs, and this section reviews the data behind the credit_default package version 1.0 on that basis [[reg:SR26-2:IV.1]].
 2| 
 3| ### Missingness within and between splits
 4| 
 5| The training split holds 3500 [[art:2510d49d:profile.train.n]] rows and the test split holds 1500 [[art:2193cf5f:profile.test.n]] rows.
 6| The largest missing fraction over any column of the training split is 0 [[art:050a3099:profile.train.missing.max]].
 7| The largest missing fraction over any column of the test split is 0 [[art:f813848d:profile.test.missing.max]].
 8| The comparison the rule draws between the two splits is a difference rather than a ratio, and because the two maxima stand at the same value that difference cannot reach the bound of 0.1 [[art:9cce25ea:threshold.D1.missing_gap]].
 9| Neither split therefore carries a missingness pattern that the other does not.
10| 
11| ### Population and characteristic stability
12| 
13| Population stability between the training split and the test split, feature by feature, is as follows.
14| 
15| - f_age: 0.008124 [[art:5017e61e:psi.f_age]]
16| - f_bill_mean_6m: 0.007124 [[art:c519fca2:psi.f_bill_mean_6m]]
17| - f_bill_trend_6m: 0.00958 [[art:c3f51172:psi.f_bill_trend_6m]]
18| - f_delinq_count_6m: 0.002069 [[art:6a2fba4e:psi.f_delinq_count_6m]]
19| - f_delinq_last: 0.00285 [[art:9d44627e:psi.f_delinq_last]]
20| - f_delinq_max_6m: 0.005498 [[art:05bccd03:psi.f_delinq_max_6m]]
21| - f_limit_bal: 0.01095 [[art:1932cef9:psi.f_limit_bal]]
22| - f_pay_ratio_last: 0.004966 [[art:f85ffaec:psi.f_pay_ratio_last]]
23| - f_pay_ratio_mean_6m: 0.0055 [[art:4d206390:psi.f_pay_ratio_mean_6m]]
24| - f_utilisation: 0.004244 [[art:b8b6b215:psi.f_utilisation]]
25| 
26| The score itself shifts between the two splits by 0.007023 [[art:a2885abf:psi.y_score]], which is smaller than the shift seen in the most displaced input.
27| The largest population stability index across the features and the score together is 0.01095 [[art:381b2570:psi.max]], carried by the credit limit feature, and it sits below the declared bound of 0.25 [[art:278b9016:threshold.S1.psi]].
28| The package file declares the same bound at 0.25 [[art:fbb5a9d1:threshold.package.psi.max]], so the validation rule and the package agree on what the population shift was allowed to be.
29| 
30| Characteristic stability, measured as each feature's contribution to the shift in the linear predictor, is as follows.
31| 
32| - f_age: 0.0009476 [[art:7eca72ca:csi.f_age]]
33| - f_bill_mean_6m: 0.002369 [[art:a56ef25e:csi.f_bill_mean_6m]]
34| - f_bill_trend_6m: 0.00633 [[art:e6bbd7a6:csi.f_bill_trend_6m]]
35| - f_delinq_count_6m: 0.002449 [[art:5c1ddd21:csi.f_delinq_count_6m]]
36| - f_delinq_last: 0.02363 [[art:dadfe01c:csi.f_delinq_last]]
37| - f_delinq_max_6m: 0.0008965 [[art:20767939:csi.f_delinq_max_6m]]
38| - f_limit_bal: 0.001211 [[art:810ae3c7:csi.f_limit_bal]]
39| - f_pay_ratio_last: 0.001924 [[art:f337e4e5:csi.f_pay_ratio_last]]
40| - f_pay_ratio_mean_6m: 0.001768 [[art:ff31f4b4:csi.f_pay_ratio_mean_6m]]
41| - f_utilisation: 0.004042 [[art:b9d55682:csi.f_utilisation]]
42| 
43| The largest characteristic contribution is 0.02363 [[art:e56cb179:csi.max]], and it comes from the most recent delinquency feature at 0.02363 [[art:dadfe01c:csi.f_delinq_last]].
44| That largest contribution is above the largest population index of 0.01095 [[art:381b2570:psi.max]], so the feature that moves the predictor most is not the feature whose marginal distribution moves most, and both remain below the declared bound of 0.25 [[art:278b9016:threshold.S1.psi]].
45| The ordering is worth noting for monitoring: a feature can shift little in its own distribution and still carry the larger share of the movement in the score.
46| 
47| ### Leakage screens
48| 
49| The declared-timing screen counts features declared as observed during the performance period or after the outcome, and that count is 0 [[art:742bcd24:leakage.timing.n_flagged]].
50| The strongest single feature reaches an area under the curve of 0.6831 [[art:fd829fc4:leakage.target_corr.max_single_feature_auc]], below the bound of 0.9 [[art:c29e7a34:threshold.L1.single_feature_auc]] that any one feature is allowed to reach on its own.
51| That margin is wide, and no individual input behaves like a restatement of the target.
52| 
53| The contamination screen runs two arms, and each is read against its own bound.
54| The first arm measures the share of test rows whose identifier also identifies a row of train, and that share is 0 [[art:63d37fc5:leakage.overlap.ids]], below the declared bound of 0.005 [[art:9f336eaf:threshold.L2.overlap]].
55| The second arm measures the share of test rows whose feature values also appear in train, and that share is 0 [[art:0fec8048:leakage.overlap.features]].
56| The second arm is read against the bound that rule actually applied, 0.005 [[art:1ee888c5:threshold.L2.overlap.features_effective]], which is the larger of the declared overlap bound and a multiple of the share of train rows whose feature values are not unique within train.
57| That construction exists because two different subjects writing the same discrete row is coincidence rather than contamination, so the bound relaxes when the training data itself repeats feature vectors.
58| Here the share of train rows whose feature values are not unique within train is 0 [[art:4474c227:leakage.duplicates.train]], so the applied bound of 0.005 [[art:1ee888c5:threshold.L2.overlap.features_effective]] is the declared bound of 0.005 [[art:9f336eaf:threshold.L2.overlap]] rather than a relaxed one, and the feature-vector arm was judged on the stricter of the two readings available to it.
59| The overlap screen over test rows records 0 [[art:4c9fcd09:leakage.overlap]], consistent with the feature-vector arm.
60| 
61| The name screen matches feature names against a target-adjacent lexicon and returns 0 [[art:407e62be:leakage.name_screen.n_matched]] matches, so no feature is named in a way that suggests it encodes the outcome.
62| 
63| ### Assessment
64| 
65| Every data check reviewed in this section returns a value inside the bound it was read against, and the two contamination arms were each read against the bound that belongs to them.
66| The residual concern is not a breach but a ceiling: the stability evidence here covers the training split against the test split only, and the shift observed there is small enough that it says little about how the population will move once the model is in use.
67| Ongoing monitoring should therefore continue to track the population and characteristic indices against the same declared bound of 0.25 [[art:278b9016:threshold.S1.psi]], with attention to the most recent delinquency feature, which carries the largest share of the movement in the linear predictor.
